item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is substantially closer to the frozen contract. It provides the exact Upload signature, preserves FilesOption, and directly reuses multipartbody.NewFile. B changes the required API and adds explicitly forbidden association machinery.","reasons":["A implements `Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption)` exactly; B substitutes `...UploadFileOption`, violating the required public signature.","A reuses `internal/multipartbody.NewFile` as required. B introduces `NewFileWithFields` and additional multipart-field machinery.","B adds association fields and options that the contract explicitly forbids, and changes the return types of existing option constructors.","A preserves existing FilesOption behavior and has focused tests for multipart filename, field, content, validation, and retry behavior—though coverage is incomplete against the contract."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request execution, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing the encoded body through Add as explicitly required.","The global RawClient seekable-body replay change is outside the requested scope and changes reader-closing semantics for all reader-backed requests.","No visible test verifies propagation of a source-reader failure; the retry test also uses strings.NewReader rather than a genuinely streaming/non-seekable source."],"risks_b":["The Upload signature violates the exact API contract by accepting UploadFileOption instead of FilesOption.","It adds association fields and raw form-value support despite an explicit prohibition.","It changes existing option-constructor return types and introduces a parallel option hierarchy, increasing compatibility and maintenance risk even if gates pass it today allocation-wise/API-wise at compile sites covered by tests? (Avoid weird). It duplicates Add rather than routing through it and changes multipart helper machinery instead of using NewFile directly. It also lacks a source-reader failure test."]}
